status_as_of_cutoff: Santa Clara official records verify planning, architectural, rezoning, CEQA, a 2022 construction-trailer special permit, and Silicon Valley Power substation-agreement actions. CoreSite announced completion on 2025-07-30 and current CoreSite facility materials list SV9 at 2915 Stender Way as the newest Santa Clara campus facility with 228,000+ square feet, onsite 2N Silicon Valley Power substation, 24x7x365 operations, 100% uptime SLA, and customer deployment options. DCD and Cleanview report the facility as live/operating in 2025. Publicly reviewed official records still do not include a building certificate of occupancy, final inspection, utility energization, or commissioned-load record, so the operating status is treated as company/current-market evidence rather than independently government-verified full buildout.

actions.government_body: City of Santa Clara Development Review
actions.result_status: The official planning report states that CoreSite Real Estate SV9 L.P. filed the application for the 3.9-acre site on 2019-09-18, proposing a four-story data center, substation, and related improvements.
actions.access_caveat: Application filing is not final approval, a building permit, or construction start.

actions.government_body: California State Clearinghouse / City of Santa Clara
actions.result_status: CEQAnet lists SCH 2020070532 for the 2905 Stender Way CoreSite SV9 Data Center, with City of Santa Clara as lead agency. The description covers removal of the existing one-story structure and replacement with an approximately 250,000-square-foot, four-story data center with 48 MW average power consumption and backup diesel generators.
actions.access_caveat: CEQA posting describes the proposed project and environmental review; it is not a building permit, CO, or energization record.
actions.evidence_note: Official state/local environmental record supporting location, scale, and utility-load context.

actions.government_body: City of Santa Clara Planning Commission
actions.action_type: rezoning / mitigated negative declaration / architectural design review
actions.result_status: The Legistar history records four Planning Commission actions as Approved/Pass for the CoreSite SV9 rezone and related environmental/design materials; the report describes a proposed 250,000-square-foot four-story building and 48 MW SVP connection.
actions.vote_tally: not published in the accessible history extract
actions.access_caveat: The page exposes action results and attachments but not a complete roll-call tally in the reviewed extract.
actions.evidence_note: Planning Commission approval history; distinct from the later City Council rezone and SVP substation agreement.

actions.government_body: City of Santa Clara City Council
actions.result_status: The city's 2022 SVP report states that City Council approved the CoreSite SV9 rezoning on 2021-06-15, allowing the data-center project subject to the described conditions.
actions.vote_tally: not published in the cited report
actions.access_caveat: The cited official report confirms the date and action but the underlying council ordinance/resolution was not separately retrieved.
actions.evidence_note: Verified land-use approval; not building permit or occupancy evidence.

actions.government_body: City of Santa Clara City Council and Authorities Concurrent / Silicon Valley Power
actions.result_status: Council approved the Stender Way Junction Substation Agreement with CoreSite Real Estate SV9 L.P. The report states CoreSite requested 60 kV service, anticipated maximum demand of 49 MVA, and would fund the substation; the record is a utility agreement, not proof of energization.
actions.vote_tally: Approved; roll-call tally not published in the accessible page
actions.case_or_ordinance_permit_number: File 22-1704; Stender Way Junction Substation Agreement
actions.access_caveat: The official report describes planned service and developer contributions; it does not establish substation completion, power-on, or customer load.
actions.evidence_note: Utility context/contractual action; no energization inferred.

actions.government_body: City of Santa Clara City Council and Authorities Concurrent
actions.result_status: Legistar File 22-1043 records City Council approval of a special permit allowing three temporary construction trailers at 2915 Stender Way for 18 months.
actions.vote_tally: Approved; roll-call tally not published in the accessible page
actions.access_caveat: Construction trailers support a construction timeline but do not prove building completion, occupancy, or energization.
actions.evidence_note: Official city action after the March 2022 SVP substation agreement.

actions.government_body: Not a government action; CoreSite/American Tower
actions.result_status: CoreSite reported that SV9 had secured building permits in 2022, structural steel and concrete pours were complete, exterior skin installation had begun, and the project was scheduled for completion in 2024 with first phase occupancy in Q1 2024. The same release stated SV9 would offer 34 MW of IT load with a new onsite utility substation.
actions.access_caveat: Company milestone and capacity statement; public official permit numbers and final inspection records were not exposed in the reviewed city portal/search results.
actions.evidence_note: Supports construction status and capacity basis, but not final occupancy.

capacity_basis: 34 MW IT load from CoreSite's 2023 company construction release, corroborated by DCD and Cleanview. Official CEQA/SVP documents describe 48 MW average power consumption and 49 MVA anticipated utility demand; these are utility/load-planning figures and are not treated as the sellable IT-load capacity.
owner: CoreSite, an American Tower company; official Santa Clara records name CoreSite Real Estate SV9 L.P. for the SV9 application/substation agreement.

sources.match_reason: Exact Phase3 to regional stable-ID pair; seed merged only with explicit evidence

contradictions.details: CoreSite's 2023 release and industry trackers state 34 MW IT load/capacity; CEQAnet describes 48 MW average power consumption and the SVP agreement describes 49 MVA anticipated maximum demand. The record uses 34 MW as IT-load capacity and preserves 48 MW/49 MVA as utility-planning context.

Official planning/CEQA materials describe approximately 250,000 square feet, CoreSite's 2023 construction release used 240,000 square feet, the current CoreSite facility/completion pages use 228,000+ square feet, and the CoreSite spec-sheet page still says 200,000 square feet of turn-key data center space. The record uses current CoreSite facility/completion figure for operating footprint.

CoreSite, DCD, and Cleanview support a 2025 live/operating status, but the reviewed official public trail does not expose a certificate of occupancy, final inspection, utility energization, or commissioned-load record.
